question: redirects
answer:
HTTPX leaves `follow_redirects` off by default. In both `Client` and `AsyncClient`, `send()` calls `_send_handling_auth()`, which delegates to `_send_handling_redirects()`. That loop uses `_send_single_request()` for each hop, populates `response.history`, and checks `Response.has_redirect_location` for a redirect status and a `Location` header. [httpx/_client.py](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:964) · [httpx/_models.py](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_models.py:772)

`_build_redirect_request()` calls `_redirect_url()` to resolve `Location`, `_redirect_method()` to choose the HTTP method, `_redirect_headers()` to adjust headers, and `_redirect_stream()` to carry or drop the body. A 302 or 303 becomes `GET` except for `HEAD`, and a 301 changes `POST` to `GET`. A 307 or 308 preserves the method. [httpx/_client.py](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:475)

With `follow_redirects=True`, the loop reads the redirect response and sends the new request, raising `TooManyRedirects` if the limit is exceeded. Otherwise, it returns the redirect response with `response.next_request` set for manual follow-up. [httpx/_client.py](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:1679)
